reason: The star’s core hydrogen is the natural starting fuel for building its layered interior.

choice.with: Hydrogen nuclei in the stellar core

expectation: Hydrogen fusion should advance the star toward a helium-rich core.

effect: Hydrogen fusion produced a helium-rich core, suggesting compression may drive its next stage.
reaction: The distinction between the core and the star was useful.
reason: Compression can heat the helium-rich core and potentially initiate its next fusion stage.
expectation: The compressed core should become hot enough for helium fusion.

effect: Compression initiated helium burning, making the core ready for its next fusion products.
reaction: The temperature distinction clarifies why ordinary chemical heat is insufficient.
reason: Helium is the visible fuel to try with the helium-burning core.
expectation: Helium fusion should produce heavier material in the core.

effect: Helium burning produced carbon-rich material through the triple-alpha process; the next stage likely builds on it.
reaction: The unstable intermediate makes the carbon-making step interesting.
reason: The carbon-rich material is the new product, but its next compatible partner is not obvious from the visible board.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how to advance the stellar interior.

effect: The carbon-rich material can combine with helium or core compression; both are plausible next stages.
reaction: The two options leave the sequence somewhat uncertain.
reason: Helium can fuse with carbon to make oxygen, so this is a plausible next step in building heavier material.
expectation: Helium fusion with carbon should produce oxygen-rich stellar material.

alternatives.reason: Compression might instead initiate the next burning stage.

effect: Helium capture produced oxygen-rich material, while compression remains a known option for the carbon-rich material.
reaction: It is satisfying to see ingredients for later rock and water emerge.
reason: Compression was a listed partner for the carbon-rich material and may advance it to the next burning stage.
expectation: Compression should advance the carbon-rich material toward a later fusion stage.

effect: Compression advanced the carbon-rich material into carbon-burning layers, producing several heavier elements.
reaction: The multiple reaction channels are an interesting detail.
reason: The next partner for the carbon-burning layers is not yet clear, so inspection should reveal how to advance them.
expectation: Inspection should identify available partners for the next stage of the stellar interior.

effect: Inspection automatically advanced the carbon-burning layers to oxygen-burning layers through compression.
reaction: The progression through hotter burning stages is becoming clearer.
reason: Further core compression has repeatedly advanced the burning stages and may continue the sequence.
expectation: Further compression should advance the core toward a later burning stage.

effect: Compression produced silicon-burning material and was consumed; its reactions move nuclei toward the iron group.
reaction: The distinction between a reaction network and a single fusion reaction is useful.
reason: The next partner for the silicon-burning material is not clear, so inspection should reveal how to proceed.
expectation: Inspection should identify a way to advance toward the end of fusion support.

effect: Silicon-burning material currently has no available partner, so I need to work with the other stellar products first.
reaction: That was unexpected for the apparent final burning stage.
reason: The carbon- and oxygen-burning layers look like complementary parts of the layered interior.
expectation: Combining the layers may build the star's layered interior.

alternatives.reason: The star might reveal how the layers fit together.

effect: Combining the burning layers built the layered interior; the remaining goal concerns the core’s loss of fusion support.
reaction: The onion metaphor usefully shows that the burning regions coexist.
reason: Silicon-burning material may advance the layered star toward an iron-group core.
expectation: The silicon-burning material should help bring the core toward the end of fusion support.

effect: The silicon-burning material brought the layered star to an iron-group core, completing the remaining goal and showing why further fusion cannot sustain it in the same way.
reaction: The connection between iron-group buildup and the loss of fusion support was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the layered interior was most worthwhile: the onion metaphor clarified that different burning regions coexist within one star.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting silicon-burning material was briefly unproductive because it had no available partner; I then had to look elsewhere for the missing prerequisite.

surprise.text: I was surprised that silicon-burning material could not be used immediately, despite appearing to be the last burning stage. The other layers first had to be combined.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt clearly arbitrary, though the need to assemble the other layers before using silicon-burning material was not initially obvious.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the approaching core collapse and see how the newly made elements contribute to later worlds.
